## Purpose

Follow-up to #32032 and closes #33708.

PR #32032 added the pipeline to publish CPU images to Docker Hub
(`vllm/vllm-openai-cpu`). This PR updates the CPU installation
documentation to recommend the Docker Hub images instead of the AWS ECR
images.

## Changes

**`docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.x86.inc.md`**
- Replace `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-cpu-release-repo:latest` with `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest`
- Add example for pulling a specific versioned tag
- Update Docker Hub gallery link (replacing ECR gallery link)
- Update `docker run` example to use Docker Hub image name

**`docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.arm.inc.md`**
- Replace `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-arm64-cpu-release-repo:latest` with `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-arm64`
- Update versioned tag from `vllm-arm64-cpu-release-repo:v${VLLM_VERSION}` to `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v${VLLM_VERSION}-arm64`
- Update Docker Hub gallery link
- Update `docker run` example

## Docker Hub Image Tags (from annotate-release.sh)

| Tag | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest` | Multi-arch manifest (x86_64 + arm64) |
| `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v<VERSION>` | Multi-arch manifest, specific version |
| `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64` | x86_64 only |
| `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-arm64` | ARM64 only |

## Test Plan

- Verified image names match the publish commands in `.buildkite/scripts/annotate-release.sh`
- Docker Hub repository: https://hub.docker.com/r/vllm/vllm-openai-cpu/tags

## Checklist

- [x] Documentation update only (no code changes)
- [x] Image names verified against release pipeline scripts
- [x] Both x86 and ARM docs updated

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in #pr-reviews, coordinate on features in #feat- channels, or join special interest groups in #sig- channels.

Just a reminder: PRs would not trigger full CI run by default. Instead, it would only run `fastcheck` CI which starts running only a small and essential subset of CI tests to quickly catch errors. 

You ask your reviewers to trigger select CI tests on top of `fastcheck` CI. 

Once the PR is approved and ready to go, your PR reviewer(s) can run CI to test the changes comprehensively before merging.

To run CI, PR reviewers can either: Add `ready` label to the PR or enable auto-merge.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.

🚀
Fixed the failing DCO check by rewriting the branch to ensure every commit has a Signed-off-by line (and dropping the merge commit). CI is re-running now.

## Code Review

The pull request successfully updates the documentation for CPU Docker images to reference Docker Hub instead of AWS ECR. The changes are clear and align with the stated purpose of migrating the image references. The documentation now provides updated commands for pulling and running the images, along with the correct Docker Hub gallery links.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

For consistency with the ARM documentation (`cpu.arm.inc.md`) and to explicitly indicate the architecture, consider using the `latest-x86_64` tag instead of the multi-arch `latest` tag. While the multi-arch tag should resolve to the correct image, being explicit can prevent potential confusion or unexpected behavior for users.

```suggestion
docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64
```
